plan.title: AD lesional vs control hallmark GSEA (Python)
plan.analytical_narrative:
The research question asks only which hallmark pathways are enriched in the treated (atopic dermatitis lesional) versus control comparison, starting from the DESeq2 results table that was already delivered (/data/inputs/results/de_results.csv, 12000 genes x 8 columns: gene, base_mean, log2_fold_change, log2_fold_change SE, stat, p-value, padj). No new differential test is fitted — that would be unasked scope and would risk disagreeing with the delivered table. The plan is therefore three steps in Python only, as the user requires.

T1S1 is the sample-level check the enrichment inherits its input from: the delivered Salmon gene-level counts (counts.csv, 12000 genes x 12 samples plus the gene id column) and metadata.csv (12 samples x 2 columns, 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch) are read, size factors and a blind variance-stabilizing transform computed with pydeseq2, PCA on the 500 most variable genes and a Euclidean sample-distance heatmap drawn, coloured by condition. This exists because the profile flags sample_01 with a library size about 4x below the median: the step reports its library size and detected-gene count beside the other 11 and shows where it sits on the PCA, but does not remove it — removal would require a stated reason and would not change the delivered results table anyway. Its purpose is to qualify how much confidence the enrichment result deserves, not to change the input.

T2S1 is the analysis that answers the question. Preranked GSEA (gseapy.prerank, the Python realization of fgsea) on the FULL list of 12000 tested genes ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the `stat` column) against the MSigDB human hallmark collection, 50 sets, release 2026.1, present in the reference store as HGNC symbols. The Wald statistic is the stated side of the disputed ranking-metric choice: it is signed and scaled by its own standard error, so a low-count gene with a large noisy log2 fold change does not float to the top, and unlike a signed -log10 p it does not tie genes whose p-values saturate. The list is never thresholded before the test. Set size window 15-500 after intersecting each set with the tested genes, BH adjustment, a fixed seed since permutation p-values are not reproducible without one. Because the input is a delivered table, the step must state the contrast direction (treated/AD lesional vs control as reference; positive stat = higher in treated) explicitly, because every NES sign depends on it. Identifiers: the results table carries gene symbols and the hallmark GMT carries HGNC symbols, so the two spaces already agree; the step reports the share of tested genes that matched no hallmark set rather than silently dropping them. GO BP/CC/MF (MSigDB 2026.1) and human WikiPathways (2026.07.10) are in the store and are run as an optional secondary pass with each release named, kept separate from hallmark — never merged, since a pathway in two collections is one finding tested twice. Reactome is NOT in the store; the step says so rather than substituting.

T1S3 assembles the report: the significant hallmark sets with NES, p, padj and leading-edge genes with their Wald statistics, the leading-edge overlap between reported sets (redundant sets collapsed to one representative), the QC verdict on sample_01 carried forward as a caveat on interpretation, and the full reproducibility record — collection name and version, rank metric, size window, seed, package versions. It states plainly that enrichment results are method-dependent and that a hallmark hit is a hypothesis for follow-up, not a proven mechanism.

gseapy preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic with MSigDB Hallmark
Enrichment report with leading edge, collection versions and reproducibility record

flags.message: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.

If fewer than about 50 genes pass the significance threshold, do not run an over-representation test on that list. A hypergeometric test of a short list finds no category, and a change of the threshold changes the list and the result. Run the ranked method on the full list of tested genes instead, because it finds a set of genes with a small but coordinated change that no single gene shows. State the size of the significant list in the report.
